paragraphs.text: In a district of a Dutch town the traffic signs were taken down in 2003. There were no lights, no crossings and no lines on the road; drivers, cyclists and walkers shared one flat surface.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Accidents fell. Drivers, no longer told what to do, slowed down and looked at other people instead of at signs. Average speed dropped by about a third, although journeys took only a minute longer.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: The idea has limits. It works in small centres with slow traffic, but the same design on a busy road increased confusion, and blind pedestrians reported that they could not tell where the pavement ended.
paragraphs.label: C
